profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite cluster spans Los Angeles, San Jose, Santa Clara, and Santa Clara County, California, the company founding home turf. Wikipedia coverage states CoreSite was established in 2001 as CRG West, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. In May 2007 the company acquired Santa Clara land for a planned 50 megawatt data center as part of a wider expansion that also added Boston and Chicago properties. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. As of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with Los Angeles and San Francisco/San Jose/Santa Clara both listed among its key markets. American Tower completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite publishes 320,000 square feet of technical space for this downtown San Jose facility and no IT-load megawatt figure on its spec page. Without a published power number, the site cannot be ranked among the five California campuses on this reference for which megawatts are known, and it does not contribute to the 170 MW total those five represent. Square footage alone does not translate cleanly into power density, because the ratio between floor area and IT load varies widely depending on cooling infrastructure and tenant mix, so no rack or accelerator estimate is offered here.

The six certifications qualify this campus for specific categories of workload. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attest to audited controls over financial reporting systems and general security operations, respectively. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments. HIPAA qualifies it for protected health information. ISO 27001 certifies a formal information-security management system. NIST 800-53 alignment positions the facility for government and regulated-sector tenants with federal control requirements. Together the certifications describe a compliance-heavy positioning, not a raw compute-scale positioning.

In California context, this site is one of 103 facilities mapped in the state, and it sits in the group that publishes no megawatt figure, placing it outside the ranked set entirely. The five facilities that do publish power figures account for 170 MW among them, and this campus's contribution to state AI capacity is unknown from public data. San Jose is geographically central to Silicon Valley demand, but grid headroom, utility interconnection, and available power for this specific address are not published, so the site's ceiling for AI scaling cannot be assessed from the operator's own specifications.
